title: AI Media Scout — hair cards, local editors and interactive stories
summary: An expanded open-ended search across creative AI, with full guides completed from earlier screened entries and additional eligible discoveries retained in the searchable pending-profile appendix. This is documentation/source review; no discovered application was installed or run. First profiles do not mean a launch today. Quality labels reflect evidence, not popularity. Incomplete evidence remains Quality unverified; current prototype or unfinished-state evidence is required for Experimental. Software, model weights, assets, hosted services and required proprietary hosts are distinguished. All platforms are researched; each guide reports the supported route rather than inferring universal compatibility. Verified collection: 887/887 repository queries attempted; 887 successful, 0 partial, 0 failed and 85 bounded/truncated. All 25 model tasks were attempted; 0 failed. These are bounded discovery attempts, not an exhaustive census or quality approval. Empty model-source responses: text2text-generation. An empty response does not establish that these creative workflows have no tools. Separate from successful search queries, 45 watchlist fetches and 3 enrichment attempts failed; the detailed warnings remain in the report. A 404/409 is an availability gap, not proof of abandonment or license revocation. Collection was resumed after an execution interruption before an observation was saved. Proven retained query/model responses and hash-matched README captures were reused with their capture times; the one missing repository query was attempted normally. Remaining repository, release and commit checks resumed live. No sealed edition or email was rebuilt or resent.

category_notes.text: Invoke documents a canvas workflow for image generation and editing. Photon AI Studio is separately screened here as an open companion for a proprietary image-editor host; neither an attractive interface nor a local-processing claim establishes output quality.

OpenReelio presents its editing workflow on its own site. This edition completes several different local/cloud editing guides and records their actual service and hardware differences rather than treating every browser editor as offline.
OpenSuno describes YuE-based music work. ZONOS3-Mini has a current model card, but its full LICENSE request returned 404; a model-card Apache label alone was not accepted as a complete grant review.
SolidCraft has its own current project site. The old SolveCraft repository redirects to the already-cataloged canonical project, so it was not added as a second new tool.
The WebLLM paper describes in-browser model inference. Browser inference is a possible implementation route, not evidence that every browser media tool supports every operating system or GPU.
Meta documents agent-assisted Immersive Web SDK development, and Google publishes a current Three-Live announcement. WebXR authoring and actual headset compatibility remain separate checks.

Fragment remains a useful creative-coding context, but conventional shader/live-code tools do not automatically qualify as AI software. Each admitted tool needs its own concrete model or agent workflow.
ossia describes interactive-installation workflows; SAT separately documents live generative-video tools. An interactive media feature alone is insufficient for AI eligibility.
SOMA documents a Windows CAD preview, while Kerfline describes image-to-laser-SVG iteration. Mesh or vector export does not establish fabrication readiness or a successful physical cut.
ForgeAX documents agent-assisted game creation. Creative AI use, reproducible export and required game-host/service terms need separate evidence from general agent branding.

Movens Zero presents motion-generation research. This edition also completes the Video Motion Customization guide, keeping the shipped combined train/infer route separate from promised standalone modes.

The AVTR-1 primary model page separates avatar-model artifacts from application code. Digital Human is profiled here with mock/default, cloud voice and optional real lip-sync routes clearly distinguished.
A primary Light-Aware Compositing PDF was captured, but a captured PDF is not a reproduced compositor or a full implementation/license review. No recommendation follows from the paper link alone.

The Neural Acoustic Fields PDF capture was bounded. A separate NSF primary publication record establishes the immersive-audio research context, while software availability and spatial audio reproduction remain unverified.

The primary volumetric-capture abstract describes RGB/RGB-D reconstruction to point clouds and Gaussian splats. Representation export is not proof of complete human capture, hardware compatibility or independently checked fidelity.

Subtitle Edit maintains its own documentation. Caption Studio receives a full guide here with the actual MLX versus Linux/Docker transcription routes, port discrepancy and optional translation services disclosed.
The SVGRender primary model organization was inspected as a discovery source. A model page does not by itself establish an installable, fully licensed vector-design application.

VecGlypher has a primary research PDF, whose bounded capture was not treated as a full paper review. This edition completes separate print-linebreak and template-typography agent guides with their actual host dependencies.

The DramaI project shell and a failed documentation URL do not establish usable released software. StoryGen receives a full guide; the recovered narrative query additionally led to source/grant-screened graph gamebooks, branching video stories and a visual fiction editor. Mock outputs and real provider calls remain distinct.

OpenSlides failed its TLS fetch. The primary manimvox documentation was accessible through its GitHub-hosted documentation URL, while its custom domain failed; this is a source-access gap rather than evidence the project is abandoned.

The primary restoration abstract addresses damaged historical color photographs. Restoration plausibility and faithful archival recovery are different claims; unseen details must not be presented as recovered facts.
The deep-learning scientific-visualization survey supplies adjacent research context. A survey is not an eligible application or evidence that an individual visualization is accurate.
MIT Media Lab provides an Illuminate project description. This establishes installation context, not a complete software grant or an independently reproduced installation.
SAT Koaia documents live generative video and a Linux/Windows NVIDIA CUDA setup. Its documentation gives model-specific GPU guidance; a GUI or a camera input does not establish Mac support.
OpenTryOn documents a local-model registry and several execution routes. Model counts and platform claims still require per-model license, hardware and result checks.

W3C audio-description guidance supplies accessibility practice context, not an AI tool. AWAS is profiled as a wearable media prototype with dependency and public-MQTT gaps, not a validated emergency aid.
MediaPipe publishes Android image-segmentation instructions. That mobile SDK route does not make a desktop generative workflow run natively on a phone.
The KinoDraw project URL returned 404. Neural Sonata is separately reviewed as a language-probability audiovisual teaching sketch; no missing education project was inferred to have shipped.
PyPottery has current suite documentation for archaeological image/document workflows. Preservation-related code, model/data terms and claims about faithful reconstruction must be checked separately.

MAESTRO describes agentic music-to-dance editing, while task documentation suggests useful adjacent search terms. A newly observed task does not establish an open-source implementation or recommendation.

The TouchTwin abstract describes phone-scan-to-editable-haptic-scene research. TactileDreamFusion is profiled separately; a normal map is not proof of physical texture, printable displacement or a reproduced tactile sensation.

NeRAF provides a primary neural acoustic research page, and AudioStellar exposes a current GitLab README. Acoustic reconstruction, corpus navigation and end-user spatial playback are different workflows.

OpenMagia has a primary project page, while OpenSlides was unavailable in this fetch. This edition screens actual scene, edit and media-agent implementations and excludes repositories containing only plans or screenshots.
The LyriFont project page describes lyrics-driven visual generation. Its student-project description provides creative context; maintained software and a complete grant need their own checks.
MAESTRO describes structure-aware, editable music-to-motion work with an agent. Published motion examples do not establish motion-capture fidelity, production rig compatibility or independent use.

Ink Blossom describes an AI-assisted embroidery installation. ZigZag is separately profiled for agent-driven design edits and conventional stitch export; a digital stitch preview is not a successful sew-out.
TMD Studio exposes notation/editing controls and Algomus publishes a GitLab research README. Conventional notation features are not AI eligibility; actual model/agent behavior is assessed separately.
AEGIR describes inverse rendering of area emitters, but its project page labels code as coming soon. It remains research context, not a newly admitted released tool.
The AromaGen primary abstract investigates language-to-olfactory composition. A paper result is not evidence of a downloadable licensed smell-authoring application or validated material safety.

AgenticCAD advertises exact CAD/CAM interaction, but its primary page explicitly limits use to non-commercial purposes. It is excluded from the open-source software selection despite creative relevance.

AEGIR provides adjacent lighting research, with code still announced rather than released on the observed page. Light-field representations and conventional environment lighting are not interchangeable.
Neural Puppet research describes learning cartoon animation from drawn examples. Muppet Stage is separately profiled with its implemented action-script, hosted speech and lip-sync pipeline.
PyPotteryTrace publishes suite-specific instructions. Ceramic-workflow relevance does not imply every component is neural or that a traced form is a verified ceramic fabrication model.
The AgenticCAD primary page states non-commercial use. This restriction blocks admission as an open-source code tool even when B-rep/STEP and agent capabilities are attractive.

A primary MapStory PDF was bounded and an alternate URL failed. LLM MapBook was separately screened for its actual book-to-place extraction and interactive mapping workflow; geocoded narrative places still need factual verification and map/book rights review.

FORM describes identifying material laws for robot manipulation, but code/data release availability remains a gap on the observed project page. Research relevance alone does not create a usable robotic-art tool.
OpenToonz supplies official animation-software context. Conventional 2D animation production does not itself qualify as AI; neural or agent capabilities require a separate cited implementation.
Fol.AI presents synchronized sound-effect research and examples, with code availability still announced rather than verified here. Paper demos were not substituted for a released grant and setup.

The TQCodec abstract describes a music-focused neural audio codec at 44.1 kHz and higher streaming bitrates. Published codec metrics are not an installed creator-facing application or independent listening test.
Sonify describes Parallax as neural moving-image art with data sonification. Neural Sonata is separately profiled for a concrete language-probability-to-sound mapping.
Brain2Music describes reconstruction from brain activity. It is specialized research context, not proof that a consumer EEG music app reads thoughts or reproduces that method.
VideoNeuMat describes neural material extraction from generative video. Material estimates, training data, renderer compatibility and practical output quality remain separate evidence checks.
A primary Neural Cameras paper was captured with a bound. No full paper read, executable release or supported capture hardware was inferred from that bounded file.
The Learn2Fold abstract discusses geometric and kinematic constraints in origami. A generated fold plan is not proof of physical foldability, released software or collision-free fabrication.
LibreTerrain provides open terrain-authoring context, but the inspected documentation did not establish a qualifying AI function. Landscape adjacency alone was not used to admit it.
Visual Anagrams demonstrates diffusion-generated multi-view illusions and jigsaw examples. These are useful mosaic/perceptual-art directions, while model terms and print alignment remain separate.

Visual Anagrams provides primary galleries of transformed multi-view images. Developer examples establish a demonstrated creative direction, not independently checked illusion robustness for every transformation.
Imprimatur describes a conventional roller-generation workflow. Its media/fabrication relevance does not establish AI functionality, so it was not admitted on that basis.

The primary painting abstract distinguishes stroke structure from final-image generation. A structured painting representation does not establish an actual robot-painting or brush-control installation.
HueForge Studio documents a Unity palette/color workflow and optional AI generation. Unity host requirements and that optional AI route must be identified separately from conventional recoloring.

The Library of Congress describes computer-vision-assisted creative exploration of digital collections. Collection rights, generated composition and faithful archival description remain separate checks.
The primary stereoscopic style-transfer abstract emphasizes left/right disparity consistency. Two independently stylized images do not establish comfortable or geometrically consistent stereo output.

The original Semantic Gaussians URL was a redirect shell; its working primary project page was also captured. Open-vocabulary scene understanding does not by itself establish editable object removal or a complete authoring application.
PHOSA describes a Chinese Sign Language avatar benchmark co-designed with Deaf experts, but the observed page still announces code release. A benchmark/demo is not a ready multilingual signing tool.
Primary Neural Amp Modeler plugin and Embedded Amp sources reveal distinct plugin/embedded routes. Model capture, audio-host compatibility and redistribution rights need per-tool evidence.

World-Shaper describes geometry-aware editing in the equirectangular panorama domain. Its examples do not by themselves establish navigable geometry, a released end-user application or headset compatibility.

Learning-Based Animation of Clothing for Virtual Try-On links models/code and describes learned drape/wrinkles trained on simulated dressed characters. Garment fit, physical cloth accuracy and model/data permissions remain separate checks.

X-Dub advertises visual-dubbing research, but the observed release wording is inconsistent about code availability. It remains a source-verification gap until an actual release and grant are established.

Morphic reshoot-anything publishes a video-to-video model card with camera-control and novel-view tags. That model card is not a complete software grant review or proof of an editable 4D reconstruction application.
Open Image Denoise and the Blender manual document render-denoising routes. A denoiser suppresses estimated noise; it does not establish scene correctness or recover true missing detail.

A primary audio-deepfake abstract distinguishes neural-codec artifacts from ordinary post-hoc compression; NuGet separately lists TensorStack.Media versions through 0.14.8. Neither detector scores nor a package release establish creative-output quality.
Imprimatur is a conventional production context rather than an established AI tool. Color, halftone, resolution and physical printing readiness require workflow-specific evidence.
AlayaWorld provides a primary world-generation research page. A video or simulated scene is not evidence of an editable, distributable game level with documented engine integration.
RAVE supplies primary neural-audio context for live patching. Training, real-time CPU/GPU requirements and patch-host support are separate from an offline audio demo.
The caustic-design primary source supplies a computational-optics research direction. Numerical light-pattern output is not proof that a fabricated optic reproduces it.

The OpenSpace planetarium AI-pilot abstract reports a study with seven professional guides and describes missing skills for live shows. A conversational camera pilot is a distinct workflow from dome calibration or edge blending.

StitchFoundry documents an embroidery direction and ZigZag has an actual MCP design interface. The separately screened embroideryai script uses palette clustering/hatching; its output is not itself a machine stitch file.
The Imprimatur context is conventional fabrication. AI eligibility and physical print quality require separate implementation and material evidence.
Nasjonalmuseet discusses local AI search, while ZKM and LinkedCulture supply museum/media contexts. Collection search, curatorial claims and generated exhibition media are assessed as different uses.
The Eagle Animation site returned only a minimal title shell. That response did not establish current AI functionality, a full software grant or a new eligible stop-motion tool.
SoundPlot provides a primary ecological-audio exploration direction. Classifier labels and visual summaries do not establish ecological ground truth or installation sound rights.

The primary anamorphosis abstract describes images whose intended form appears through a particular viewpoint or catadioptric device. Digital examples do not establish a calibrated mirror/lens installation or complete released software.
Primary light-field research is relevant to view-dependent displays. A rendered sequence does not establish compatibility with a particular lenticular or Looking Glass display.
The AstroSURE abstract studies denoising low-photon astronomical images without clean targets. Attractive denoising is not evidence that faint structures are astronomically real.
The primary tactile-graphics abstract explicitly separates screen realism from haptic/physical constraints. Generated reliefs still need accessibility and fabrication evaluation.
UDnet provides an author gallery, weights and code links for neural underwater color/contrast enhancement. Natural-looking color does not establish calibrated scientific color recovery.
A primary acoustic-holography conference PDF was captured but not fully parsed/read in this pass. No released implementation, acoustic hardware compatibility or measured sound field was inferred.
CalliRewrite provides handwriting-behavior reconstruction research with code links. Recovered trajectories do not establish a calibrated robot, ink or paper workflow.
ComicTL documents browser-local bubble detection, OCR and translation with WebGPU. Local processing claims, model rights and translation fidelity remain separate review items.
ShopPrentice documents an OAuth-protected hosted MCP furniture-design service. Its public endpoint does not establish an open-source standalone woodworking application.
Taarib publishes an agent-based Arabic localization template. Game access/rights, engine-specific text handling, fonts and executable-patching behavior need separate checks.
LacyLights documents DMX/Art-Net theatrical control with optional agent integration. AI-authored cues still need human fixture, timing and physical rig checks.
Music2P describes multimodal album-cover generation. An album cover is an adjacent layout practice, not evidence of a complete multi-page photobook imposition tool.
WAIvePulse documents local music generation, a studio and looper. Offline generation, loop seam quality and model licensing are separate questions.
The primary yarn-modeling abstract infers procedural fiber-level parameters from an image. It does not establish a machine-knitting pattern or validated yarn/fabric fabrication.
StegaStamp supplies primary learned watermarking context. A detectable watermark is not proof of ownership, tamper resistance in all print/camera conditions or universally robust provenance.
Deep Halftoning documents learned descreening/rescreening. A separate inverse-halftoning PDF capture was bounded; it was not treated as a full paper or software review.
BrickGPT links the BrickWright follow-up and demonstrates text-to-brick structures. Claimed buildability still needs actual part inventory, connectivity and physical stability checks.

Stanford/Princeton primary pages document several neural holography approaches. SGWN Encoder is separately profiled for numerical phase encoding, with optical assumptions and checkpoint redistribution uncertainty explicit.

RiTa v4 explicitly describes itself as AI-free and was not admitted merely because it generates language. J-space theater and Neural Sonata instead expose concrete AI probability/hidden-state creative workflows; an empty jhave.com capture remains a gap.

HairDeck and its independent ComfyUI integration support a concrete image-to-hair-card workflow. HairGS combined non-commercial terms, missing grants and promised releases kept several other hair projects outside the eligible selection.

HyFluid and PICT smoke reconstruction have actual research/code context, but complete software grants were not returned for the inspected repositories. Smoke demos or paper availability did not override this licensing gap.

ecosystem_checks.finding: Current raw project documentation and grants were read for JoyAI MLX, openedit and an Xotion license. The first two are already profiled, so unchanged projects were not relisted. Xotion retains a complete PolyForm Noncommercial grant and is excluded. A live video-editor topic listing was a discovery aid, not license proof.

Imaginer metadata and the Raspberry Pi diffusion project were accessible. Broader diffusion/audio exploration requests returned HTTP 429; those failed attempts are archived and were not bypassed. Project availability is not a completed current license/setup review.

The live diffusion project search returned diffront, diffuser and prs-search. The complete Diffuser MIT grant and Cargo manifest were read; its dependency points to an author-local absolute path, so portability remains a setup gap. The existing screened entry was not relisted unchanged.

Live npm/PyPI/NuGet metadata was archived, including litert-ocr 0.2.2, manimvox, brandly and TensorStack.Media through 0.14.8. Registry classifiers and license labels are discovery signals, not complete grants or independent quality evidence. No package was installed.

Krita and SAT primary documentation supplement plugin discovery. HairDeck integrations are screened for their actual node execution/export paths; underlying model terms and ComfyUI/platform requirements remain separate. A proprietary-host companion is labeled explicitly.

Current primary sites were fetched across all 102 observed fields. Several sites returned 404/TLS failures or empty shells and several PDFs were bounded; these are disclosed per field, not treated as complete implementation reviews. The pass is broad and bounded, not an exhaustive census.

Primary papers/project pages supplied hair, fluid, holography, tactile, motion and adjacent creative leads. Actual code and full grants were inspected separately: HairGS combined non-commercial terms and missing PICT/HyFluid grants blocked eligibility; code-coming-soon projects stayed context/watch findings.

Korean/English print typography, Japanese VR HTML authoring, Chinese creator workflows and Arabic game-localization documentation were inspected. Native-language docs are not a reason for a weaker or stronger quality label; licenses, host services and platform recipes remain explicit.

watchlist.name: HairGS
watchlist.reason: The root MIT file does not supersede the additional non-commercial Gaussian-Splatting terms that the README says apply to the combined distribution. It is creative research context, not an admitted open-source application.

watchlist.name: DiffLocks
watchlist.reason: The complete grant limits use to non-commercial scientific/educational/artistic purposes and restricts redistribution. A separately MIT-licensed subcomponent does not make the complete project open-source.

watchlist.name: Crayotter
watchlist.reason: The full root grant is PolyForm Noncommercial; paper wording about openness does not replace that software restriction.

watchlist.name: IPHG / CT2Hair / HairPort
watchlist.reason: The inspected root grants are CC BY-NC or CC BY-NC-ND. These non-commercial/no-derivatives restrictions do not qualify as open-source software grants.

watchlist.name: SAFE-Hair / NeuralHDHair / HairGPT
watchlist.reason: A promised release or paper/project page does not establish a complete released and licensed application. Actual inference availability and full grants remain unresolved for these candidates.

watchlist.name: HyFluid / PICT smoke
watchlist.reason: Actual research code was located, but complete software grants were not returned for the inspected repositories. Smoke reconstruction examples were not substituted for license evidence.

watchlist.name: VRMHairMaker
watchlist.reason: The project has HairDeck-related implementation but no complete own software grant was returned. An upstream Apache grant is not automatically a grant for the wrapper.

watchlist.name: StrandHead
watchlist.reason: An MIT root sits alongside borrowed NeuralHaircut material with separate non-commercial terms. The full combined source/provenance scope requires resolution before admission.

watchlist.name: FengLairh ComfyUI-HairDeck distribution
watchlist.reason: The adapter root is Apache-2.0, but this distribution vendors SAM 3 and DINOv3 software under custom licenses covering code as well as weights, including use restrictions. It is held pending a clearly separated open-code scope; mirrors and checksum validation do not remove license conditions.

watchlist.name: Comfy-WebUI / wan-pilot
watchlist.reason: The full Apache-looking grants alter the standard liability wording. They were not automatically treated as recognized Apache-2.0 merely because metadata identifies that SPDX value.

watchlist.name: Mia full-guide completion
watchlist.reason: The application root is Apache, but bundled model/graph components have separate community and open-source grants and some models are non-commercial or research-limited. The existing historical screened entry is preserved; this edition does not assert an all-Apache bundle or publish a completed guide without resolving the selected component scope.

watchlist.name: AgenticCAD
watchlist.reason: The primary page explicitly states free for non-commercial use. Creative relevance and CAD export do not establish an open-source software grant.

watchlist.name: Xotion Studio
watchlist.reason: The complete GitLab grant is PolyForm Noncommercial, so this otherwise relevant video project is excluded from open-source software results.

watchlist.name: AEGIR / Fol.AI / PHOSA / FORM
watchlist.reason: The primary pages describe relevant research but announce code/data as coming soon or leave release availability unresolved. Paper/video examples are not evidence that a licensed implementation has shipped.

watchlist.name: RiTa v4
watchlist.reason: The primary site explicitly describes the toolkit as AI-free. It is useful generative-language context, but conventional language generation alone does not meet this library AI-only scope.

watchlist.name: Missing or unreleased implementations
watchlist.reason: Some searched repositories contained only architecture/docs, planned neural features or screenshots/binary releases. Those were not admitted merely from an AI label, root license or executable download; raw candidate details remain local for later source checks.

watchlist.name: MoneyPrinterPlus
watchlist.reason: The complete root LICENSE appends personal/educational-only and no-commercial-use conditions to a GPL-looking text. These restrictions exclude the combined grant despite GitHub GPL metadata.

watchlist.name: OpenDesign
watchlist.reason: The full license changes Apache trademark wording and the additional-liability/support section. Its Apache metadata and large star count were not substituted for a recognized unmodified grant review.

watchlist.name: TeaCache composite grant
watchlist.reason: The full root license includes a large composite set of upstream notices/grants. A complete composite review remains pending; the first Apache header was not treated as the whole license.

watchlist.name: No-Slop Color
watchlist.reason: The official current repository metadata marks this project archived. It is not admitted as a currently maintained discovery; the reviewed MIT license and creative-use source evidence remain retained locally. Archive status alone does not revoke its license or judge all historical output.
